title: Multi-tenant AI platform
description: Teams call one gateway that checks their quota, applies a guardrail, retrieves from the company's documents and calls a model. Documents flow in through a queue. Each team keeps its own data.

detail.role: The single public entry point for every team.
detail.why: One front door keeps authentication, quota and logging in one place.

detail.role: Identifies the calling team, checks its token budget and model allow-list, then hands the request to the router.
detail.why: Teams never hold a provider key and cannot exceed their budget.

security.text: Each request is tied to one team before anything else happens.

cost.text: Token budgets are checked before a model is called, not found on the invoice.

detail.role: Applies the guardrail, retrieves passages for the question, chooses a model and returns the answer.
detail.why: Cheap models handle easy work; the expensive one is kept for what needs it.

risks.text: A rule that sends hard questions to a weak model lowers quality without an error.

detail.role: Blocks unsafe input and output.
detail.why: Safety rules are the platform's, not each team's.

detail.role: Finds the passages most related to a question.
detail.why: Answers come from company documents, not the model's memory.

detail.role: Stores the numeric form of each document passage and finds the closest to a question.
detail.why: Matches on meaning, not just on shared words.

detail.role: The company documents the knowledge base indexes.
detail.why: One shared corpus, encrypted, with versions of its own.

security.text: Conversations are encrypted with the platform key and expire by TTL.

detail.role: Holds each conversation so a follow-up question has its history.
detail.why: The router stays stateless and can scale freely.

detail.role: Which teams exist, their budgets and allowed models.
detail.why: Onboarding a team is a row, not a deployment.

detail.role: The key that encrypts documents, queues and conversations at rest.
detail.why: One key under platform control: access can be withdrawn in one place.

detail.role: Holds documents waiting to be indexed.
detail.why: A burst of uploads does not overload the indexer; failures retry.

detail.role: Receives documents that failed indexing five times.
detail.why: A bad document is set aside for a person, not retried for ever.

detail.role: Takes documents from the queue, reads them from the bucket and has the knowledge base index them.
detail.why: Indexing runs in the background, apart from the request path.

detail.role: The router's logs.
detail.why: Needed to explain a wrong answer after the fact.

detail.role: Notifies the on-call engineer when the router's error alarm fires.
detail.why: Failures are found by the platform before a team reports them.

detail.role: Runs each team's services in its own namespace, sharing one set of machines.
detail.why: Teams deploy without owning servers, and the platform sets the guard rails once.

detail.role: The machines the team services run on.
detail.why: Capacity grows and shrinks with load; teams do not manage servers.
A team's private documents are never mixed with another team's.

detail.role: Where a team submits documents it wants searchable.
detail.why: Each team has its own queue, so one team's backlog cannot delay another's.

detail.role: Each team's services, running in the shared cluster with their own identity.
detail.why: Not created by this Terraform, so drawn from the overlay.

detail.role: Writes the answer from the question and the retrieved passages.
detail.why: Called by model id, not created by this Terraform.

detail.role: How a team joins: a template creates its registry entry, its buckets and queues, and its identity.
detail.why: Joining the platform is a pull request, not a project. Not created by this Terraform, so drawn from the overlay.

addLinks.label: Chat request
addLinks.detail: A team's service calls the platform API with its own identity.

addLinks.label: Generate
addLinks.detail: The question and retrieved passages go to the chosen model; the answer streams back.

addLinks.label: Own documents
addLinks.detail: Each team stores its private documents in its own bucket.

addLinks.label: Submit for indexing
addLinks.detail: A team queues documents it wants searchable by the whole company.

addLinks.label: Create team
addLinks.detail: Onboarding writes the new team's budget and allowed models into the registry.

trace.label: A team's service sends a question
Its budget and allowed models are read from the registry
The router asks for related passages
The vector index returns the best matches
Passages go back to the router
The router picks a model for this task
The conversation is saved for follow-up questions

layers.label: Golden path
layers.summary: The one supported way in: what a team uses to start and to call the platform.

layers.label: Control plane
layers.summary: Decides and governs: team registry and budgets, safety policy, keys, logging and alerts.

layers.label: Runtime
layers.summary: Does the work for each request and each document: gateway, router, retrieval, models, ingestion.

layers.label: Tenants
layers.summary: What each team owns: its applications, its private documents and queues, and the cluster they run on.
